simple.meaning: הוֹדִיָּה (Hôwdîyâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “Hodijah , the name of three Israelites.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: הוֹדִיָּה (H1941) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Nehemiah 8:7, with occurrences in Nehemiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הוֹדִיָּה (H1941) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in הוֹדִיָּה (H1941) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: הוֹדִיָּה (Hôwdîyâh) / H1941 is traced through Nehemiah 8:7, Nehemiah 9:5 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

timeline.evidenceText: Also Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites, caused the people to understand the law; and the people stayed in their place.

Then the Levites, Jeshua, and Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah, said, “Stand up and bless Yahweh your God from everlasting to everlasting! Blessed be your glorious name, which is exalted above all blessing and praise!
